gaps.sentence: She put her ideas ___ clearly and confidently.
gaps.explanation: put across = communicate an idea successfully.

gaps.sentence: We need to iron ___ a few details before signing.
It took the committee weeks to wade ___ the paperwork.
gaps.hint: wade ___ = plod through a lot of
gaps.explanation: 'Wade through' = work slowly through a large amount of tedious material.

gaps.sentence: Do you get ___ well with your new colleagues?
gaps.explanation: get on (with) = have a good relationship; also get along with (AmE).

gaps.sentence: The new manager wants to back ___ the sales team's proposal.
gaps.explanation: back up = support (a person, plan); also make a copy of data.

gaps.sentence: A new proposal was put ___ at the meeting.
gaps.explanation: put forward = propose, suggest (an idea, plan, name).

gaps.sentence: I fell ___ with my best friend over a silly remark.
gaps.explanation: fall out (with somebody) = have an argument and stop being friendly.

gaps.sentence: The meeting has been ___ off until Thursday.
gaps.explanation: 'Put off' = postpone to a later time.
